Direct Harbor recovery trial

Diagnostic only. Production evaluation and Pages remain unchanged.

Download machine-readable results · Frozen input manifests · Workflow evidence excerpts

Decision

Address one specific blocker before the live pair: native Codex workspace-write sandbox compatibility with the existing unprivileged Docker/runner boundary. The grading smoke passed; adoption and skill effectiveness remain unproven.

Two expected native grades recovered: good detects 2/2 seeded defects; weak detects 0/2 despite passing the reference. No codex exec task or paid inference occurred. Production remains unchanged.

These are deterministic oracle controls, not live model evidence. Each final control has one valid observation. Both suites execute three tests and pass the reference; only the good suite detects both defects. The earlier missing-submission result remains ungradeable. Raw native carriers and submitted work are in the linked Actions artifacts and retained local evidence; this bundle contains reviewed metadata only.

Neither live variant ran. Four actual Codex sandbox-helper probes executed without credentials; no codex exec task or provider inference occurred. Activation, instruction following, skill effectiveness and efficiency/regressions remain unmeasured. No skill revision was created or authorized in this recovery.

Campaign usage

Cumulative paid attempts: 0/36; recovery: 0/4 maximum. Cumulative API spend: $0 because no credential or model call was used, not because missing telemetry became zero. Oracle token/cost observations remain null. The $20 operational budget is not a provider cap. A future pair is conservatively estimated at $1.44 for two 60k-input/4k-output attempts, charging all input including cache at $10/M and output at $30/M. The proposed $4 scheduling stop leaves $16 reserve; in-flight overshoot remains possible. Unknown usage stops further scheduling. No paid accounting control was exercised.

Sandbox and deployment boundary

The actual helper used workspace-write, approval_policy=never, inner network disabled and temporary-directory write exceptions excluded. The probe first checks UID 1000, zero effective capabilities, no-new-privileges, no Docker socket and an ordinary outside-workspace write. Exact helper commands, errors and return codes are retained in sandbox.json.

Bubblewrap reports namespace creation denied under the tested Docker/runner restrictions; the exact enforcing kernel/seccomp/AppArmor mechanism was not isolated. The explicitly tested deprecated Landlock backend rejects this policy as requiring direct runtime enforcement. Neither probe reaches its intended inner write/network assertions, so the inner boundary is not qualified.

The outer container kept default seccomp, cap_drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, CPU/memory/PID limits and no host Docker socket. The sandbox probe was offline; a live API-connected agent did not run. Codex inner sandbox and outer container protection are separate. No protection was relaxed.

Harbor import_path is the supported extension point. The small trial subclass replaces the stock bypass flag with --sandbox workspace-write -c approval_policy=never, requires the pinned preinstalled CLI and uses a build-owned private home. The transformation is unit tested; no effective live command/config was produced. No installed upstream file changed.

Execution and supporting artifacts

  • Recovery build preflight — Failed before Harbor started: snapshot 503/504 responses and a 600-second image-build timeout. Failure record retained. · Build failure · Image unavailable
  • First native control — Oracle exit 126: script lacked executable permission. Verifier invalid/artifact remains unmeasured. Default sandbox helper was missing; legacy policy rejected. · Native invalid result · Sandbox errors
  • Final native controls and sandbox checks — Good passes and weak fails as expected. Overall workflow failed because both sandbox probes failed. · Known-good pass · Known-weak fail · Sandbox blocker

History

Original run 41952213509 explicitly received a runner shutdown signal. Cause remains unknown; exit 143 alone does not identify a Harbor timeout/crash. No original native grade survived. Its prior report is preserved as history below; the prior recommendation is superseded and does not show that the existing stack is better.

Maintenance and remaining evidence

Recovered grading evidence is useful: both suites pass the reference, but only the good suite detects both mutants. The earlier numeric zero reward with a missing submission remains ungradeable. This validates the narrow pass/fail distinction, not all legitimate or adversarial submissions.

The projection delegates failure cause and reward validity to pinned Harbor, preserves native exceptions/verifier observations and excludes unsupported or missing evidence. Ten tests cover correct/incorrect work, agent timeout with valid grading, provider/environment/verifier failures, handled step failures, unknown usage and post-run failed status/exit.

Custom maintenance: staging/projection/reporting, 10 focused tests, a 47-line Codex subclass, 34-line native sandbox probe, 29-line snapshot transport helper and one branch-only workflow. No framework patches. The adapter depends on the stock launch string and three pinned helper methods and needs review on Harbor/Codex changes. The transport helper is another component to retain only while needed.

Existing tasks, reference implementations, mutants, grader, PowerShell runner and runtime installer were reused unchanged. Another skill still needs representative inputs, independent good/weak submissions and a protected executable verifier. Lower total maintenance cost has not been demonstrated.

Production components removed: none. Only overlapping behavioral wrapper/staging/collection layers could become removable after broader adoption evidence. APM deployment, static checks, graders, historical evidence and publication controls remain necessary.

Smallest next step: qualify one supported native Codex sandbox configuration under the same required outer boundary without disabling protections. Then run the current/absent pester-002 smoke pair. Do not start the original full comparison yet.
